Package org.apache.juneau.marshall.parser

Class MissingRequiredPropertyException

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Throwable
java.lang.Exception
java.lang.RuntimeException
org.apache.juneau.commons.BasicRuntimeException
org.apache.juneau.marshall.BasicRuntimeException
org.apache.juneau.marshall.parser.ParseException
org.apache.juneau.marshall.parser.MissingRequiredPropertyException
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class MissingRequiredPropertyException extends ParseException
Thrown when parser input (or the source map of a Map-to-bean conversion) does not contain one or more properties marked @BeanProp(required=true).

The check runs once per bean, after all input properties have been read and before the bean is constructed, so records and constructor-argument beans get this exception instead of a constructor failure. An explicit null value counts as present.

This is a ParseException, so REST @Content parameters map it to 400 Bad Request.

Example:

public record Person(@BeanProp(required=true) String name, Integer age) {} try { JsonParser.DEFAULT.read("{\"age\":30}", Person.class); } catch (MissingRequiredPropertyException e) { e.getBeanClass(); // Person.class e.getPropertyNames(); // [name] }

  • Method Details

    • check

      public static <T> BeanMap<T> check(ParserSession session, BeanMap<T> m)
      Throws this exception if the bean map is missing required properties.

      Parser sessions call this through ParserSession.checkRequired(BeanMap). Conversion code that has no parser session passes null, which omits the input position from the message.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The bean type.
      Parameters:
      session - The current parser session, or null if not parsing.
      m - The bean map to check. Can be null.
      Returns:
      The same bean map, for chaining.
      Throws:
      MissingRequiredPropertyException - If a required property was never written.

    • find

      public static MissingRequiredPropertyException find(Throwable t)
      Finds a MissingRequiredPropertyException in the cause chain of a throwable.

      Bean property setters wrap failures from nested conversions, so conversion code uses this to re-surface the original exception (which is a ParseException and maps to HTTP 400).

      Parameters:
      t - The throwable to inspect. Can be null.
      Returns:
      The first exception of this type in the chain (including t itself), or null if none.
